references.text: Matthew's list of the twelve apostles also mentions Judas Iscariot as the one who betrayed Jesus.
Mark's list of the apostles mentions Judas Iscariot and describes him as the one who betrayed Jesus.
John identifies Judas, son of Simon, Iscariot, as the one who was to betray Jesus.
Judas Iscariot, son of Simon, had already been put in his heart by the devil to betray Jesus.
Judas—not Iscariot—is mentioned here, distinguishing him from Judas Iscariot. This Judas is likely the same as Judas, son of James, mentioned in Luke 6:16.
The Acts of the Apostles mentions Judas, son of James, among the apostles who were gathered in the upper room after Jesus' ascension.
Peter speaks about Judas Iscariot, who betrayed Jesus, and who was counted among the twelve and had a share in this ministry.
The Epistle of Jude is written by Jude, brother of James, whom many identify with Judas, son of James, mentioned among the apostles.
